papers.title: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Introduction: In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. Methods: We analyzed 57 plasma samples from stable patients with HCM and 10 plasma samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma cfDNA was isolated from both groups. Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) libraries were generated and sequenced with short-read sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. Results: Yields of cfDNA (p = 0.003) and cfDNA-CM (p = 0.002) fractions were higher in AMI controls than HCM, supporting the validity of the assay. Within the HCM cohort, the median cfDNA yield was 12.22 ng [IQR: 7.77, 18.94]. The cfDNA-CM fraction in this cohort ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI, p=0.001), a greater prevalence of BMI 30 kg/m2 (p<0.001), and a higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in other demographic, genetic, and laboratory characteristics. Higher cfDNA-CM tertile was numerically associated with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, while circulating biomarkers of wall stress (NT-proBNP) and myocardial injury (troponin) did not differ across tertiles (p=0.83 and p=0.29, respectively). Conclusion: Isolation and quantification of cfDNA as well as detection of cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM are feasible. Higher cfDNA-CM fraction was associated with increasing BMI and cardiometabolic comorbidity burden. The absence of association with traditional circulating biomarkers suggests that cfDNA-CM may reflect a distinct domain of myocardial health, injury, and adverse remodeling.

papers.title: Feasibility of continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video in a hypertension clinic cohort: the BP-WAVE pilot study
papers.abstract: Introduction. Whether the arterial pressure waveform carries structural vascular information that brachial pressure does not, and whether its shape can be read from facial video, are both uncertain, and recording a continuous pressure reference with synchronised video in a hypertension clinic has not been reported. We sought to determine whether continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video, linked to existing coronary calcium imaging, is feasible in adults attending a hypertension clinic, whether a consumer camera recovers heart rate and pulse shape in that setting, and to generate exploratory estimates of association between waveform morphology and coronary calcium. Methods. BP-WAVE is a single-site prospective observational pilot study. The primary outcome was feasibility, pre-specified as recruitment, consent, completeness of waveform recording, imaging availability and data completeness. Secondary outcomes were waveform quality, device agreement, feature extraction, and recovery of heart rate and pulse shape from video. The exploratory outcome was the Spearman correlation of 14 waveform features with the Agatston calcium score, with exact permutation p values adjusted within each family of tests. Results. Nine of ten planned participants were recorded over 12 days (median age 55 years, range 40 to 74; five women); all nine completed the recording with video and had a calcium score (median 351, range 33 to 1816). Of 4,178 detected beats, 2,965 (71%) passed quality control. Video recovered heart rate within 0.4 to 4.1 beats per minute in eight of nine participants and pulse shape above a phase-randomised noise bound in six of nine (held-out r 0.48 to 0.76). Form factor had the strongest correlation with calcium (rho -0.68, exact p 0.050, q 0.68); no feature was associated with calcium after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within any of the nine families of 14 tests (126 tests in all; smallest q 0.17). Conclusion. In this single-site pilot of nine adults from a hypertension clinic, continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video and linkage to coronary calcium was feasible, a consumer camera recovered heart rate in eight and pulse shape in six participants, and no waveform feature was associated with coronary calcium after correction for multiple testing.

papers.title: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
papers.abstract: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. Methods: An ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. Results: Internal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. Conclusions: FM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Stationarity in Predicting TEVAR Response
papers.abstract: Background: Hypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes. Methods: Blood pressure (n = 560) and HR (n = 680) time-series data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on time-series data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes. Results: Successful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes. Conclusion: Post-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

papers.title: Temporal Trends and Demographic Disparities in Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Utilization in the United States, 2016-2022
papers.abstract: Condensed Abstract: Using the 2016?2022 National Inpatient Sample, this study evaluated temporal trends and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). Among 190,020 weighted procedures, annual volume increased from 4,875 to 60,445. In-hospital mortality was exceptionally low (0.1%). Age-adjusted procedural rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population. However, significant disparities persisted, characterized by heavy centralization in urban teaching hospitals (87.0%) and disproportionately lower absolute age-adjusted utilization among female, Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Pacific Islander patients compared to male and White cohorts. Targeted initiatives are needed to ensure equitable access to structural heart interventions.

papers.title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
papers.abstract: Background: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a major complication of chronic right ventricular pacing and develops in up to 25% of patients. Reliable prediction of PICM may facilitate individualized pacing strategy selection; however, currently available approaches demonstrate limited discriminative performance. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting PICM in patients with atrioventricular block (AVB) underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. Methods: In this multicenter prospective study derived from the RISK-PICM registry (January 2002 to January 2026), 125 patients with AVB who underwent pacemaker implantation were analyzed. PICM was defined as a ?10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) resulting in an LVEF <50%. Four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost, were trained using stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter optimization and model discrimination was evaluated. Results: PICM developed in 41 patients (32.8%) during a median follow-up of 4.8 years. Male sex, pre-implant minimum QTc interval, and post-implant maximum QRS duration were significantly associated with PICM in univariable Cox regression. XGBoost achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.831; sensitivity 0.805; specificity 0.845). Feature importance analysis identified baseline LVEF and post-implant maximum QRS duration as the most influential features. Model-derived risk stratification significantly differentiated high-risk and low-risk groups on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P < 0.001). Conclusions: ML-based models, particularly XGBoost, demonstrated clinically meaningful performance for PICM and may support individualized pacing strategy selection in patients with AVB and underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.

papers.title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
papers.abstract: Standard cardiac biomarkers such as ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, and strain compress complex three-dimensional heart dynamics into a small set of predefined measurements, leaving clinically important heterogeneity unrecognised. Here we propose a personalised normative cardiac framework in which each individual is compared to a digital twin representing expected healthy cardiac function given their age, sex, and body habitus. We show that structured patterns of deviation from these normative twins, discovered through systematic exploration of a generative cardiac dynamics space, constitute novel dynamic phenotypes that are not captured by conventional biomarkers. Applied independently to two UK Biobank cardiac cohorts with distinct shape representation, a 128-dimensional four-chamber statistical shape descriptor (HeartSSM, n = 52,365) and a 64-dimensional deep generative latent space from a conditional variational mesh autoencoder (MeshHeart cVAE, n = up to 39,376), we identify reproducible, continuous deviation-from-normative-twin scores (three discrete deviation phenotypes in the HeartSSM cohort) that improve cardiovascular risk stratification beyond ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and strain. The strongest effect was seen for incident atrial fibrillation among individuals with preserved ejection fraction (at least 50%): incremental C-index delta C = +0.068 (5-fold cross-validated delta C = +0.063; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3 x 10^-8), with a separate, smaller effect for incident stroke in the same preserved-EF subgroup in the independent MeshHeart cVAE representation (which showed no signal for atrial fibrillation) (delta C = +0.024, P = 2.6 x 10^-4). Both effects were checked against placebo controls in which the deviation scores were replaced by Gaussian noise. To test whether the normative twin generalises beyond UK Biobank's specific scanning and processing pipeline, we applied the MeshHeart cVAE normative twin, unmodified, to an independent external cohort of healthy volunteers imaged at a different hospital (GenScan/Hammersmith, n = 315): deviation scores in this cohort were of comparable magnitude to the UK Biobank healthy reference (ratio of means = 1.09; Mann-Whitney P = 1.4 x 10^-5), indicating that the normative twin captures cross-site-transferable structure rather than a scanner- or pipeline-specific artefact. Our findings suggest that cardiac phenotyping can move beyond predefined measurements toward data-driven dynamic phenotypes that better capture the heterogeneity underlying cardiovascular disease risk, even among individuals whose ejection fraction appears normal.

papers.title: Serial measurements of Growth Differentiation Factor-15 in patients with Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome and recurrent ischemic events
papers.abstract: Background: Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) has emerged as a prognostic biomarker in patients with non-ST-segment-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Our study evaluated the temporal evolution of GDF-15 in the acute phase and its association with recurrent ischemic events. Methods: Serum samples were collected from patients with NSTE-ACS at admission and at 1 and 3 hours after admission. GDF-15 levels, along with other prognostic biomarkers, NT-proBNP and hs-cTnT, were measured. Spearman rank-correlation coefficients and linear regression models were used to identify the variables associated with GDF-15 levels at admission and with their temporal changes. Associations between GDF-15 and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. To assess incremental prognostic value, the areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated for each model. Results: GDF-15 levels showed a slight increasing trend within 3 hours of admission. The 1-hour change in GDF-15 was correlated with hs-cTnT changes. Increased 1-hour GDF-15 levels, compared with the admission levels, were associated with a higher risk of recurrent ischemic events during the 1-year follow-up (1.9% vs. 17.5%, P =0.019) and were an independent predictor after adjusting for established clinical variables and biomarkers (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.71 (1.28 to 228.75), P =0.03). Furthermore, serial measurements of GDF-15 provided additional prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors. Conclusions: Serial measurements of GDF-15 of NSTE-ACS patients provided independent and incremental prognostic value for predicting recurrent ischemic events. These findings support the potential utility of GDF-15 as a dynamic biomarker for early risk stratification in the acute management of NSTE-ACS.

papers.title: Age-, sex-, and ethnicity-stratified CMR strain reference ranges and centile-based categories from the Healthy Hearts Consortium
papers.abstract: Background This study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. Methods The dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42 derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Results After quality control, 8,975 CMR examinations (cvi42) and 8,992 (suiteHEART) were available for analysis; these represent software-specific analytic cohorts. Most exclusions occurred during visual quality control. Women had higher absolute ventricular and atrial strain values than men across all age groups. Left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain and strain rate were slightly lower in older ages, whereas circumferential and radial parameters remained largely stable. Left atrial strain was also lower in older age groups, while right atrial strain did not vary by age. Annular plane systolic excursion and rapid strain metrics showed similar sex-specific patterns, with modestly lower atrial and displacement values in older groups. Ethnicity-related differences were modest, heterogeneous, and substantially smaller in magnitude than age- and sex-related differences. Technical effects were parameter specific. While LV longitudinal and circumferential strains were largely unaffected, radial strain was higher at 3 T and showed vendor-related differences. LMS-derived reference ranges and centile thresholds were applied both across all ethnicities and within ethnicity-specific analyses, and are presented stratified by age and sex. In the prognostic analysis, centile categories were most consistently associated with incident heart failure. LV longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain below the 0.5th centile were associated with significantly increased risk of incident heart failure (HRs: 9.9 to 12.4, 95% CIs 7.00-13.90 to 8.49-18.06). Conclusion This study provides age- and sex-specific reference ranges and centile-based categories for CMR-derived strain parameters in a large reference population. Age and sex represent the primary determinants of myocardial deformation, whereas scanner-related effects are parameter-specific. Values in the lower extremes of the healthy reference distribution, particularly for LV strain, are associated with increased risk of incident heart failure. These findings enable standardized, centile-based classification of myocardial strain, facilitating consistent interpretation and improving risk stratification in research and clinical practice.

papers.title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation - serum-driven amplification of atrial electrical instability
papers.abstract: Rationale: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is sustained by electrical triggers and atrial substrate, but whether AF itself generates circulating factors that acutely reinforce arrhythmogenesis is unknown. Objective: To determine whether rhythm-dependent serum bioactivity directly destabilizes atrial electrophysiology and to identify associated cellular mechanisms and circulating mediators. Methods and Results: Cardiac samples were obtained from patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) during AF and after restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) using electrical cardioversion. In isolated Langendorff-perfused mouse hearts, AF serum increased the duration, frequency, and cumulative burden of spontaneous atrial depolarizations compared with paired control perfusate. In human induced pluripotent stem cell derived atrial cardiomyocytes, AF patient serum decreased Ca2-transient amplitudes without significant effect on kinetics or Ca2 spark activity. Moreover, AF serum reduced peak sodium current without materially altering voltage-dependent gating or paced action-potential properties. Data-independent acquisition proteomics identified rhythm-associated changes in extracellular-matrix, proteolytic, inflammatory, and signaling proteins, including MMP9, Ccathepsin G, and 14-3-3 family members. Targeted pathway perturbation differentially modified serum-induced Ca2 phenotypes, indicating context-dependent, multifactorial bioactivity. Serum-induced Ca2 responses were not associated with indices of atrial disease severity, including low-voltage substrate burden and left atrial pressure. Conclusions: Persistent AF is accompanied by rhythm-dependent circulating bioactivity that acutely promotes atrial electrical instability and Ca2-dependent trigger formation. These findings extend the concept that AF begets AF beyond tissue-intrinsic remodeling and identify a potentially reversible serum-mediated feed-forward mechanism linking rhythm status and circulating proteomic signals in an atrial substrate severity independent fashion. Keywords: atrial fibrillation; serum; atrial cardiomyopathy; calcium signaling; circulating factors; proteomics

papers.title: Uneven Recovery of Exercise Training in US Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors or Disease Following the COVID 19 Pandemic
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to significant disruptions in cardiovascular care and reductions in physical activity, but little is known about how exercise patterns changed after this period. This study assessed changes in weekly aerobic and strength training activity between 2020 and 2022 amongst adults aged 18 years or older who reported one or more cardiovascular diseases or risk factors. This study used National Health Interview Survey data from 2020 and 2022. Adjusted differences for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were calculated using a linear regression model and for strength sessions using a Poisson regression, adjusting for sex and age. Changes in these outcomes were then stratified by age and sex subgroups. The weighted study population included 182,783,008 (standard error, +/-3,334,337) adults in 2020 and 185,388,060 (SE, +/-3,285,161) adults in 2022. Between 2020 and 2022, the overall weekly MVPA increased from 244.2 (SE, +/-4.5) minutes to 266.3 (SE, +/-5.7) minutes (adjusted difference, +22.1 [SE, +/-6.92] minutes). There were no statistically significant changes in the number of strength session per week overall or among sex and age subgroups. Across sex and age subgroups, increases in weekly MVPA were entirely concentrated among males and younger adults. The recovery from pandemic era reductions in aerobic and strength exercise training was uneven amongst demographic subgroups, which aligns with concurrent persistent disruptions in cardiovascular care.

papers.title: Efficacy of Disease-Modifying Treatments in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Five Phase III Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.abstract: Background Several disease-modifying agents for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) have been investigated, but differences in trial design and background stabilizer use complicate interpretation of their efficacy. This meta-analysis assessed their efficacy overall and by background stabilizer use. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through September 2026 for phase III randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in ATTR-CM. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary (KCCQ-OS) score, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), pooled with a random-effects model. Treatment effects were compared between the monotherapy and baseline stabilizer strata using a mixed-effects model. Results Five trials (ATTR-ACT, APOLLO-B, ATTRibute-CM, HELIOS-B, CARDIO-TTRansform; N=3497) were included. Disease-modifying therapy reduced all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66-0.87; I2=0%) and improved 6MWD (pooled standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.20-0.67), KCCQ-OS score (SMD, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.55), and NT-proBNP (SMD, -0.53; 95% CI, -0.89 to -0.18). The mortality benefit was similar whether therapy was given alone or added to a background stabilizer (pooled risk ratio, 0.77 vs. 0.71; P for interaction = 0.59), but treatment effects on 6MWD (pooled SMD, 0.49 vs. 0.14), KCCQ-OS score (0.44 vs. 0.07), and NT-proBNP (-0.65 vs. -0.13) were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer (P for interaction = 0.012, <0.001, and 0.029, respectively). Conclusion Disease-modifying treatments reduced all-cause mortality and favored functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP outcomes in patients with ATTR-CM. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed smaller treatment effects on 6MWD, KCCQ-OS score, and NT-proBNP among patients receiving a background stabilizer, with no statistically significant difference in the mortality effect according to baseline stabilizer use.

papers.title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients. Methods In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) 2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders. Results Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p< or =0.009), with modest gains in discrimination ({Delta}C 0.007-0.009). Conclusions In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow.

papers.title: Population-scale trends and variations in human aortic biomechanics
papers.abstract: The biomechanical properties of the human aorta play a key role in cardiovascular function and disease, yet their population-wide trends and variations remain largely unknown. To fill this crucial gap, we quantified variations in aortic size, stiffness and stresses across 57,434 individuals from the UK Biobank using two-dimensional cine MR imaging and a combined deep-learning, probabilistic and biomechanical modelling framework. Aortic diameter and distensibility (inverse of stiffness) were calculated for the ascending and descending aorta, and their conditional distributions were characterised as a function of age, sex, body size and blood pressure. These observations were integrated with ex-vivo tissue mechanics to infer stress distributions across the aortic wall and the associated uncertainty. Our analysis revealed several new relationships. Larger aortas were found to be stiffer, and greater body size (height and/or weight) was associated with larger aortas with no change in stiffness. Aortic distensibility was negatively associated with systolic, but not diastolic, blood pressure. Apparent sex differences in aortic size were substantially reduced after accounting for body size. Importantly, the maximum stress was found to depend not only on aortic size, as previously thought, but also on distensibility, with lower distensibility associated with higher stresses. The results provide first-of-their-kind population-scale reference distributions for human aortic stiffness, which will improve the personalisation of computational models and digital twins. The correlation between stress and distensibility strongly supports progressing beyond the current diameter-based criteria (based on the law of Laplace) and for the inclusion of stiffness in the clinical risk assessment of aortic diseases. Overall, this study forms the foundation for personalised quantitative medicine and biomechanically informed risk stratification of aortic aneurysms and dissections.

papers.title: 30-Day Heart Failure Readmission and Post-Discharge Healthcare Use Among Older Australians: A Linked-Data Mixed-Methods Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Heart failure (HF) is a major public health challenge in ageing populations and a leading cause of unplanned hospital readmissions. Biological, social, and economic factors contribute to recurrent hospitalisation, but gaps remain in understanding how these factors interact and patterns of healthcare use following hospitalisation. Methods: We conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study of patients aged ?60 years with an HF hospital admission between 2016 and 2020 who completed the Sax Institute?s 45 and Up Study baseline questionnaire. Data were linked to Admitted Patient Data Collection, Medicare Benefits Schedule, and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data. HF readmission within 30 days of the index admission was the outcome. Cox proportional hazards models estimated crude and adjusted hazard ratios (HRs and adjHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests compared survival between groups. Time-series plots mapped healthcare interactions over 1 year following the index admission. Results: Among 4,252 patients with HF, 409 were readmitted within 30 days. Significant predictors included age ?80 years (adjHR, 1.30; 95%CI, 1.01?1.67), 1 chronic condition (adjHR, 2.49; 95%CI, 1.41?4.40), ?2 chronic conditions (adjHR, 1.75; 95%CI, 1.04?2.95), and alcohol consumption above national guidelines (adjHR, 1.45; 95%CI, 1.06?1.98). Time-series analysis indicated that participants with readmission had more frequent out-of-hospital health service contact following their initial HF admission than those without readmission. Conclusions: Older age, chronic conditions, and high alcohol intake increased 30-day HF readmission risk. Differences in healthcare use after admission highlight opportunities for targeted and coordinated post-discharge care.

papers.title: Pulsed Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation For Repeat Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation: Evaluation of Outcomes
papers.abstract: Background Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has recently been approved in the USA as a new method for treating atrial fibrillation (AF). PFA provides a promising new approach in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF), which historically has a high recurrence rate post-ablation. Of significance, PFA has shown promising data in terms of safety and procedural efficiency to radiofrequency ablation (RFA). Objective The purpose of this study was to compare the procedural and health outcomes in patients with recurrent AF undergoing ablation using PFA or RFA. Methods Consecutive patients with a history of previous radiofrequency ablation and recurrent AF undergoing redo ablation with PFA or RFA were included. Patients were seen for follow-up in the clinic ranging from 4 months to a year and we reported ablation strategy and arrhythmia type. The primary outcome was recurrence of any atrial arrhythmia after a 90-day blanking period. Results A total of 242 patients with recurrent AF underwent redo ablation using PFA (n = 54, 22.5%) or RFA (n = 188, 77.5%). The PFA cohort was younger on average (66 vs. 70 years) with a lower mean CHA2DS2-VASc score (2.2 vs. 3.06, p=0.001) compared to the RFA cohort. PFA procedures were shorter (162{+/-}53 vs 206{+/-}60 minutes, p<0.001) but required more fluoroscopy (13.9{+/-}8.9 vs 8.7{+/-}6.3 minutes, p<0.001). Among patients seen on follow-up, recurrence occurred in 28% of PFA versus 55% of RFA patients, with longer arrhythmia-free survival after PFA (log-rank p=0.03). PFA remained associated with lower recurrence after multivariable adjustment (HR 0.4, 95% CI 0.2?0.9, p=0.04). Adverse events, predominantly vascular access?related, were similar. Conclusion Among patients with recurrent atrial arrhythmias after prior RFA, repeat PFA was associated with shorter procedures, greater fluoroscopy use, and lower arrhythmia recurrence, with comparable safety.

papers.title: Pressure is not flow: Rethinking blood pressure as a surrogate for cerebral blood flow during general anesthesia
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Mean arterial pressure (MAP) is pharmacologically augmented in selected perioperative and critical care settings, including acute neurological conditions and after cardiac arrest, with the aim of improving cerebral perfusion, although it remains uncertain whether higher arterial pressure translates into increased cerebral blood flow (CBF). We investigated the CBF response to MAP augmentation with norepinephrine (NE), a commonly used vasopressor in perioperative and critical care settings, during propofol-based general anesthesia. Methods: In this prospective within-subject interventional study, 16 neurologically intact patients with ASA physical status I-II undergoing elective surgery were studied using phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging. CBF was quantified in the awake state and during propofol-based general anesthesia before and after NE-induced MAP augmentation. During general anesthesia, NE was titrated to increase MAP by approximately 25% from baseline. Concurrent systemic hemodynamics were assessed. Results: General anesthesia was associated with a 50.1% (interquartile range, 42.1?55.7%) reduction in CBF and a 24.2% (20.3-29.2%) reduction in MAP compared with the awake state (both P<0.001). During general anesthesia, NE-induced MAP augmentation increased MAP by 25.7% (21.9-32.0%; P<0.001), whereas CBF remained unchanged (P=1.000). Cardiac output remained unchanged (P=0.163), whereas systemic vascular resistance index and cerebrovascular resistance increased by 40.0% (28.7-45.2%) and 36.2% (17.7-42.8%), respectively (both P<0.001). Changes in CBF during MAP augmentation were not associated with concurrent changes in MAP, cardiac output, or systemic vascular resistance index. Conclusions: In neurologically intact patients undergoing propofol-based general anesthesia, clinically relevant NE-induced MAP augmentation did not increase CBF despite an approximately 50% lower CBF than in the awake state. These findings challenge the assumption that pharmacological elevation of an otherwise adequate MAP improves cerebral perfusion in this setting. While maintaining adequate arterial pressure remains essential, further MAP augmentation should not be assumed to increase CBF. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06855407; NCT06855407.

papers.title: Persistent Hypertension After Asymptomatic Elevated In-Hospital Blood Pressure: The INDEBP Study
papers.abstract: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) is common during hospitalization. Despite recommendations to avoid routine changes in antihypertensive therapy, clinical practice remains variable. Prospective data on whether elevated in-hospital BP identifies patients with hypertension after discharge are limited. Methods: Adults hospitalized for non-cardiac conditions with asymptomatic routine in-hospital BP ?140 and/or ?90 mmHg on at least two occasions separated by ?24 hours were prospectively enrolled. Antihypertensive therapy was managed at the discretion of treating physicians. Routine in-hospital BP, standardized research BP, and changes in antihypertensive therapy were recorded. Four weeks after discharge, participants underwent 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM). Results: Among 50 participants, 42 (84%; 95% CI, 70.9 ? 92.8) had hypertension on follow-up ABPM. Among 21 participants without known hypertension, 18 (86%) had previously unrecognized hypertension on follow-up ABPM; among 29 participants with known hypertension, 24 (83%) had uncontrolled hypertension. Antihypertensive therapy was changed during hospitalization in 26 participants (52%), with de-escalation more frequent than intensification. Hypertension on follow-up ABPM was present in 88.5% of participants with and 79.2% without in-hospital therapy changes. Standardized research BP, but not routine in-hospital BP, correlated with follow-up ABPM. Conclusion: Asymptomatic elevated routine in-hospital BP identified a population with a high prevalence of hypertension four weeks after discharge, including patients with and without previously diagnosed hypertension. These findings support structured post-discharge BP reassessment rather than assuming that elevated in-hospital BP is transient. URL: www.ClinicalTrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06132451

papers.title: A tuneable structural switch controls RNF213 activity and is bypassed in Moyamoya disease
papers.abstract: RNF213 is a giant AAA+ ubiquitin ligase that serves as a central hub of innate immunity, responding to diverse stress signals with broad reactivity1-6. This versatility demands tight regulation, and its failure causes disease, such as Moyamoya angiopathy7-10 and cancer progression11-13. How the mega-enzyme is restrained and how mutations override this control is unknown. Here, we show that RNF213 activity is regulated by a dimeric switch -- a constitutive dimer that alternates between auto-inhibited and activation-competent states. In the closed dimer, intermolecular contacts bury the E3 machinery, whereas ATP binding remodels the AAA+ core to open the dimer and prime ubiquitination. Dimer conversion is tuned by ubiquitination factors, redox conditions and post-translational modifications, allowing multiple stress signals to act through the same activation mechanism. Moyamoya mutations subvert the same open-closed transition, destabilizing the autoinhibited dimer in a graded manner that tracks with clinical severity. Structural, biochemical and cellular data reveal how disease mutations allosterically disrupt the dimer interface and bypass ATP-dependent control to drive NF-{kappa}B activation and caspase-dependent apoptosis. Together, our findings reveal a tuneable dimeric switch that converts diverse stressors into graded inflammatory signalling and provide a mechanistic link between genetic predisposition, environmental triggers and Moyamoya disease.

papers.title: Investigating the Causal Impact of COVID-19 on Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Multi-ancestry Mendelian Randomization Study
papers.abstract: Observational studies suggest an association between COVID-19 and acute myocardial infarction (AMI), however, whether this relationship is causal remains unclear. We conducted a multi-ancestry Mendelian randomization (MR) study across European, East Asian, South Asian, and African populations, evaluating three COVID-19 phenotypes: very severe COVID-19, hospitalized COVID-19, and general infection association with AMI. GWAS summary statistics were obtained from the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative Round 7 and UK Biobank/Biobank Japan for AMI. Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) MR was the primary method, with fixed-or random-effects models selected according to heterogeneity test. MR-Egger, weighted median and weighted mode were conducted as sensitivity analyses. In European ancestry, genetic liability to very severe COVID-19 and hospitalized COVID-19 was slightly inversely associated with AMI risk, but without statistical significances across sensitivity analyses. Hospitalized COVID-19 showed a suggestive but non-significant inverse association in South Asian ancestry. No significant associations were identified in East Asian or African ancestries. Our findings did not support a robust causal association between COVID-19 susceptibility or severity and AMI risk across ancestries, suggesting that the observed cardiovascular burden may be driven more by acute pathophysiological mechanisms than shared genetic architecture.

papers.title: The ARumenamide AR-788 suppresses the transient outward current in human iPSC-derived right-ventricular Brugada cardioids
papers.abstract: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmia disorder with limited drug therapy, quinidine being the principal agent. Loss-of-function variants in SCN5A reduce the cardiac sodium current (INa), but the arrhythmogenic imbalance also depends on the transient outward potassium current (Ito). Here we generated human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardioids with right-ventricular identity from a patient carrying an SCN5A frameshift variant (p.A665Gfs*16) and characterised them by patch-clamp and optical mapping. BrS cardioids showed 60% lower peak INa, more than doubled Ito, 38% slower conduction and 76% longer spontaneous cycle length. We then tested AR-788, a benzylaminothiazole- benzimidazole carboxamide of the ARumenamide class. In wild-type (WT) cardiomyocytes AR-788 inhibited Ito concentration-dependently (12%, 30% and 42% at 5, 10 and 20 {micro}M; extrapolated IC50 25.4 {micro}M), and at 10 {micro}M it returned BrS Ito to the level of untreated WT cells (21.71 vs 21.48 pA/pF, p = 0.9716) without reducing INa. It also reduced the rapid delayed-rectifier current (IKr) tail current by 40%, a liability requiring formal proarrhythmia profiling. These data identify AR-788 as an Ito-suppressing member of the ARumenamide class and provide proof of concept that a small molecule can correct the potassium-current excess in a human BrS model.

papers.title: Machine Learning Models Using Electronic Health Record Data to Predict Obstructive Sleep Apnea
papers.abstract: RationaleObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent yet largely under-diagnosed. Current screening strategies rely on effortful questionnaires with modest accuracy, and prior machine learning models often require resource-intensive inputs and lack external validation. ObjectivesTo develop and validate machine learning models to predict OSA (apnea-hypopnea index [AHI4%][≥]5) and moderate-severe OSA (AHI4%[≥]15) using only routinely collected electronic health record (EHR) data, test cross-system transferability and compare performance with clinical screeners and a Bayesian risk-updating framework. MethodsThree tree-ensemble families (XGBoost, random forests, and histogram-based gradient boosting) were trained on an adult cohort with sleep-study results at Kaiser Permanente (KPSC), using full (106-feature) and minimal (age, sex, body-mass index, race/ethnicity) predictor sets and tuned by nested cross-validation. XGBoost models were selected, internally and temporally validated, and externally validated at University of Kansas Medical Center (KUMC). Measurements and Main ResultsOn our internal hold-out set (n=53,048), the full XGBoost model reached a ROC-AUC of 0.791 for any OSA and 0.768 for moderate-severe OSA. The minimal model retained most performance (0.764 and 0.736). Temporal performance was stable. Externally, frozen models showed lower AUCs (0.718 and 0.690 for full models; 0.725 and 0.706 for minimal models) but similar to KUMC-native models and improved further with transfer learning. The models significantly outperformed STOP-BANG (AUC difference 0.06-0.09 for predicting any OSA; p<0.001). Bayesian updating with select patient-reported items further improved discrimination. ConclusionsMachine learning models based on EHR data can predict OSA probability that outperform existing screeners, transfers across systems, and offers potential for EHR implementation. At a Glance CommentaryO_ST_ABSScientific Knowledge on the SubjectC_ST_ABSObstructive sleep apnea is common and heavily underdiagnosed, yet upstream patient identification still depends on symptom and anthropometry questionnaires such as STOP-BANG, which are effort-dependent and achieve modest performance. Prior machine learning models for OSA are heterogeneous, often developed on small or demographically narrow cohorts, frequently rely on physiologic signals that reintroduce a testing step, and are rarely validated across independent health systems. What This Study Adds to the FieldWe developed machine learning models from routinely collected electronic health record data, comprising a full (106-feature) and a minimal (4-feature) model, to predict any OSA and moderate-severe OSA. The study is distinguished by multiple validation efforts, including temporal validation and external validation at a second health system. We further explored adaptation strategies for external adoption using transfer learning techniques. Finally, the models outperformed existing screeners such as STOP-BANG, and we describe a Bayesian framework that optionally incorporates select patient-reported symptoms to refine individual risk estimates. Overall, these models are feasible to implement within EHR systems as a low-effort, passive screener that can support encounter-based and population health outreach screening strategies.

papers.title: Beat-to-Beat Action Potential Duration Variability, Not Duration, Reflects β-Adrenergic Stimulation-Induced Repolarization Instability
papers.abstract: Instability of the cardiac electrical system is a major cause of life-threatening arrhythmias. Current safety guidelines have traditionally emphasized QT interval prolongation on the electrocardiogram (ECG) as a primary biomarker of proarrhythmic risk. However, this approach does not capture all forms of electrical instability. In this study, we demonstrate that beat-to-beat variability in action potential duration (APD), a cellular surrogate of the QT interval, better stratifies proarrhythmic risk than mean APD prolongation alone. Using a validated computational model of a human ventricular myocyte, we simulated the effects of the {beta}-adrenergic agonist isoproterenol (ISO). Increasing the ISO concentration shortened mean APD but paradoxically increased beat-to-beat APD variability, measured as the standard deviation of APDs. In our simulations, the emergence of early afterdepolarizations (EADs), abnormal oscillations of the membrane potential during the plateau phase of the action potential, at higher ISO concentrations was consistently preceded by a marked rise in APD variability, even while mean APD was reduced. Mechanistic analysis revealed that ISO-induced enhancement of L-type Ca2+ current (ICaL) and slow delayed rectifier K+ current (IKs) steepens the APD restitution slope, which reflects action potential instability, even when the net effect is a reduction in APD. These results support APD variability as a more sensitive and mechanistically plausible marker of proarrhythmic risk than APD prolongation alone. Our findings suggest that QT interval variability may improve risk stratification and provide a more robust mechanistic foundation for drug safety evaluation. Significance StatementQT interval prolongation remains an important component of cardiac safety assessment, but changes in mean QT duration may not fully capture the dynamic stability of ventricular repolarization. Here, we show that beat-to-beat APD variability increases during {beta}-adrenergic stimulation even when mean APD shortens, and increases further as the system approaches conditions associated with EAD formation. These findings identify APD variability as a complementary measure of repolarization stability and provide a cellular mechanistic basis for further evaluating QT interval variability as an additional marker of proarrhythmic susceptibility.

papers.title: Myocardial Perfusion in Patients with Primary Mitral Regurgitation Due to Mitral Valve Prolapse
papers.abstract: BackgroundMitral regurgitation (MR) is a common complication of mitral valve prolapse (MVP) and increases left ventricular (LV) preload, promotes LV remodeling and hypertrophy, but its impact on myocardial perfusion and coronary microvascular dysfunction remains unclear. ObjectivesTo assess myocardial perfusion using, for the first time, quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) perfusion mapping in patients with significant MR due to MVP. MethodsPatients with significant primary MR, without coronary artery disease were prospectively enrolled and compared to age- and sex-matched controls without MR. All underwent 1.5T CMR including cine imaging, adenosine stress perfusion, native T1, native T2, extracellular volume (ECV) mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Myocardial perfusion reserve (MPR) was calculated as the ratio of stress to rest myocardial perfusion. ResultsIn total 33 patients and 33 controls were included (age 56{+/-}13 vs. 58{+/-}12 years, 46% women in both groups). Patients with MR had increased LV mass and volumes, higher native T1 and ECV and a higher prevalence of LGE (36% vs 0%). No differences were observed in global myocardial perfusion at rest (0.88{+/-}0.27 vs. 0.85{+/-}0.30, p=0.52), at stress (2.6{+/-}0.56 vs. 2.8{+/-}0.73 ml/min/g, p=0.29) or for MPR (3.1{+/-}0.75 vs. 3.4{+/-}1.0, p=0.24). In age- and sex-adjusted linear regression, higher NYHA class was associated with lower MPR ({beta} =-0.60, p=0.04). ConclusionIn patients with significant MR due to MVP, myocardial perfusion appears preserved despite LV volume overload. However, lower MPR in symptomatic patients suggests that microvascular dysfunction may emerge in a more advanced disease stage.

papers.title: Post-Initiation Care Patterns and Weight Loss With Semaglutide and Tirzepatide for Obesity in Clinical Practice
papers.abstract: BackgroundRandomized trials show substantial weight loss with semaglutide and tirzepatide under structured care, but little is known about whether patients in routine practice continue therapy, reach a maintenance dose, and have their weight measured. ObjectivesTo describe the first year after initiation of semaglutide or tirzepatide for obesity, including care patterns, maintenance-dose attainment, weight documentation, and total body weight loss (TBWL). MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used Epic Cosmos, an electronic health record network of >350 US health systems, to identify adults with obesity and without diabetes who initiated injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide in 2024. Outcomes over 12 months included prescribing persistence, discontinuation, switching, add-on therapy, and reinitiation; attainment of Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-labeled maintenance doses; availability of follow-up weight; and TBWL across progressively restricted populations. ResultsAmong 743,153 adults (60.1% semaglutide; mean age, 48.5 years; 72.5% female), 12-month prescribing persistence was 29.9% for semaglutide and 35.9% for tirzepatide. FDA-labeled maintenance-dose attainment was 28.3% and 55.0%, respectively, and only 8.8% and 16.4% remained prescribing persistent at a maintenance dose with a recorded weight at 12 months. About half of initiators lacked a 12-month weight. Among all initiators, [≥]5% TBWL was documented in 25.6% (semaglutide) and 30.4% (tirzepatide), rising to 51.9% and 61.9% among those with recorded weight, 66.1% and 79.5% among those also prescribing persistent, and 82.9% and 87.3% among those further at a maintenance dose. ConclusionsIn routine practice, most patients initiating semaglutide or tirzepatide did not remain on therapy, reach a maintenance dose, and have weight documented through the first year. Documented weight loss was greatest among those completing each step of care, suggesting continuation, dose escalation, and monitoring as targets for improvement. Numbers are per 100 initiators and were rounded so that categories at each step sum to the preceding step. papers.title: Right Versus Left Ventricular Myofiber Orientation in Various Congenital Heart Diseases Analyzed with X-Ray Phase-Contrast Tomography
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDWhile the systemic right and left ventricles have different functional prognoses, only a limited number of reports have addressed their myocardial architecture. This study analyzed myofiber orientation of human specimens with various congenital heart diseases using X-ray phase-contrast tomography. METHODSThree specimens of each normal heart, ventricular septal defect, right atrial isomerism, left atrial isomerism, and ventricular inversion were examined. In reconstructed images of both ventricles, the center of the free wall was resliced parallel to the myocardial surface. A myofiber helical angle was identified in each slice and plotted from epicardium to endocardium. The plotted curves were compared between both ventricles. RESULTSIn all ventricles, the helical angle was changed from left-handed on epicardial slices to right-handed on endocardial slices. Whereas the right ventricles helical angle curves showed a plateau with or without a rapid rise on the endocardial side, the left ventricles curves had sustained increase with or without a plateau in the middle. The median wall-thickness- scaled helical angle change rates were 53{degrees} and 102{degrees} in the right and left ventricle, respectively, and their distribution of each specimen was higher in the left ventricle than in the right ventricle. CONCLUSIONS: Ventricular myofiber orientation has a consistent transmural helical transition independently of cardiac morphology and looping. Their transitions can have a plateau and rapid changes permitting the identification of layers within the ventricular wall. The left ventricle has more helical fibers and the right ventricle has more circumferential fibers, which may explain their difference of ventricular performance.

papers.title: Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return: A Multicenter Case Series.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) has been observed in adults with anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR), but data on catheter ablation outcomes in this population remain limited to case reports and small series. MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 14 adult patients with confirmed APVR who underwent catheter ablation for AF at three tertiary academic centers in the United States between July 2003 and May 2025. Baseline, procedural, electroanatomic mapping, and outcome data were collected. Freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. ResultsMean age was 56 {+/-} 13 years and 79% were male. Heart failure was present in 64%, and hypertension and coronary artery disease in 43% each. Most had partial APVR (86%), and 57% had prior surgical correction. Radiofrequency ablation was used in all patients, combined with pulsed-field ablation in one. Acute success was achieved in all patients, although areas with residual pulmonary vein or SVC electrical activity were left untreated in 3 (21%). Non-pulmonary-vein electrical activity was more common in patients with prior surgical correction than in those without (43% vs 17%). Median follow-up was 3.4 years (IQR, 2.0-9.6). Freedom from arrhythmia recurrence was 78.6% at 1 year and 53.9% at 5 years. Two patients (14%) required reablation; complications occurred in 3 (21%) without long-term sequelae. ConclusionsCatheter ablation was acutely successful in all patients in this largest reported APVR cohort, despite substantial comorbidity burden and anatomic complexity. The arrhythmogenic substrate often extended beyond the anomalous vein, particularly in surgically corrected patients, supporting individualized, substrate-guided ablation in this population. CLINICAL PERSPECTIVEO_ST_ABSWhat Is KnownC_ST_ABSO_LIAtrial fibrillation has been reported in adults with anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR), but data on catheter ablation outcomes in this population are limited to case reports and small series. C_LI What the Study AddsO_LIIn the largest reported cohort of patients with APVR undergoing catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation, pulmonary vein isolation achieved acute success in all patients despite substantial comorbidity burden and anatomic complexity. C_LIO_LINon-pulmonary-vein sites of electrical activity were more common among patients with prior surgical correction, and postsurgical scar and epicardial venoatrial connections were also arrhythmogenic, indicating that the arrhythmogenic substrate in APVR often extends beyond the anomalous vein itself. C_LIO_LIThese findings support individualized, substrate-guided mapping in patients with APVR, particularly those with a surgical history, and suggest a role for pulsed-field ablation near critical structures such as the phrenic nerve. papers.title: Convergent genetic and functional evidence implicate KCND3 in Brugada Syndrome
papers.abstract: BackgroundDysfunction of the KCND3-encoded Kv4.3 channel, which carries the transient outward potassium current (Ito), has long been suspected to contribute to the pathophysiology of Brugada Syndrome (BrS). Although recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have implicated KCND3, the role of rare variation in this gene remains uncertain and clinically unactionable. MethodsGenome sequencing was performed in 983 BrS probands from Europe and Thailand. Putative gain-of-function (GoF) rare variants in KCND3 identified in patients were functionally characterized by patch-clamp analysis of Kv4.3 current properties using a HEK293 cell heterozygous model. Biobank datasets were utilized to evaluate rare-common variant interaction at the KCND3 locus. ResultsEight BrS cases carried six different rare KCND3 variants which clustered at the Kv4.3 C-terminus, with terminal exon rare variants significantly enriched in cases versus study (p=0.004) and population (p=2.0e-6) controls. Four of the five KCND3 case variants studied demonstrated significant GoF effects versus wild-type and putative benign variants, including increased Ito amplitude (p.Leu586Val, p.Ala634Thr) and slower inactivation (p.Gly600Arg, p.Ala654Thr, p.Ala634Thr). Analysis of p.Gly600Arg carriers in the UK Biobank and All of Us revealed a significant enrichment of the protective KCND3 expression-reducing allele of the GWAS lead single-nucleotide polymorphism rs12090194, suggesting a possible epistatic common-rare variant interaction modifies penetrance in carriers. ConclusionsGoF rare variants at the C-terminus of KCND3 are associated with BrS in a small proportion of cases. Determination of the rare and common variant status in BrS patients and their relatives may provide information about disease risk.

papers.title: Procoagulant plasma in three individuals with stabilin-2 deficiency
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDRare STAB2 loss-of-function variants emerged in population studies as being associated with elevated venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk. STAB2 encodes the cell-surface scavenger receptor stabilin-2, and reduced stabilin-2 function might increase VTE risk via elevated plasma levels of its ligands, including von Willebrand factor (VWF) and coagulation factor VIII (FVIII). METHODSAn adolescent patient with dependency on parenteral nutrition had experienced episodes of central venous catheter-related thrombosis, including the complete thrombotic occlusion of the deep pelvic veins, and pulmonary embolism. Exome sequencing for increased VTE risk identified a homozygous STAB2 splice-site variant and its effect on splicing was characterized in fibroblast-derived RNA and in a minigene splicing system. Plasma VWF, FVIII, and fibrinogen and serum hyaluronic acid (HA) levels were determined. Immunohistochemistry was performed on liver biopsy tissue. RESULTSThe STAB2 splice-site variant caused aberrant STAB2 mRNA splicing. The patients healthy mother and one healthy sibling were also homozygous for the STAB2 splice-site variant but had no history of VTE. Plasma FVIII levels and VWF activity were elevated in all three, and VWF antigen was elevated in two homozygous individuals. Strikingly, approximately 1000-fold elevated HA levels were observed in all three homozygous individuals. Stabilin-2 immunohistochemistry on a liver biopsy from the probands mother revealed no detectable signal, whereas control human liver showed strong labelling of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells. The STAB2 splice-site variant thus results in loss of detectable stabilin-2 protein. CONCLUSIONSTo current knowledge, this is the first family-based report of stabilin-2 deficiency with markedly elevated circulating HA, VWF, and FVIII levels in humans. These findings support impaired stabilin-2-dependent ligand clearance as a thrombosis susceptibility state with incomplete penetrance. The data are consistent with a significant role for stabilin-2 in circulating HA clearance in humans, but do not establish elevated HA itself as a cause of VTE.

papers.title: Dendritic cells and vascular inflammation in patients with coronary artery disease with and without chronic kidney disease
papers.abstract: ObjectiveDendritic cells (DCs) are priming local immune responses, and their tissue-associated activity increases in inflammatory conditions. In patients with coronary artery disease (CAD), circulating dendritic cell precursors (DCPs) are reduced. This study investigates circulating DCPs and tissue densities of migrated DCs in CAD patients undergoing bypass surgery, focussing on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) as a risk factor for CAD and a condition of chronic vascular inflammation. Approach and ResultsCirculating DCPs were measured in the peripheral blood (before surgery) using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) in n=59 patients and results were compared with an age-matched healthy control group (n=45). DCs were stained (Fascin) in circular sections of the internal thoracic artery taken during bypass surgery and mature (CD83+) and immature (CD209+) DCs were differentiated. Cell densities were obtained digitally. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis generated hypotheses. Circulating myeloid DCPs were reduced (p<0.001), concomitant CKD added no further reduction. Immature DCs were predominantly detected in the adventitia, mature DCs dominated in the intima (p<0.001). In CKD, reduced circulating myeloid DCPs correlated with immature DCs in the vessel wall (r=0.87; p=0.002) and rather mature DCs were detectable; in patients without CKD immature DCs were dominating. C-reactive protein correlated with mature DCs (r=0.38; p=0.026). ConclusionsQuantities of DCPs and mature and immature DCs vary between the vessel wall layers. The dominance of immature myeloid DCs in the adventitia suggests activation of the vascular-associated lymphoid tissue (VALT). Intensified inflammation associated with CKD may have promoted the maturation of myeloic DCs.
